xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: The Commissioner, CGST (Appeals), vide order dated 26th November 2025, has set aside the demand order dated 28th January,2025 passed by Joint Commissioner, CGST, Noida.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The Company had received an Order of the Commissioner, CGST (Appeals) which has allowed the appeal of the Company and set aside the order of Joint Commissioner, CGST, Noida dated 28th January, 2025 wherein it had disallowed the Transitional Input Tax Credit (“ITC”) and demanded recovery of the ITC amounting to Rs. 1,92,12,510 (Rupees One Crore NinetyTwo Lakh Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Ten Only) along with an equivalent penalty and applicable interest under the provisions of the CGST / UPGST Act. As a result of the same, the demand for tax, penalty and interest now stands dropped.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: The Additional Commissioner, ACC (Import) NCH, New Delhi (“Adjudicating Authority”)
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: The Adjudicating Authority vide order dated 18th December 2025 (received on 29th December, 2025) has confirmed Customs duty demand of Rs. 32,95,005/- being duty short paid along with applicable interest and also imposed equal amount of penalty of Rs.32,95,005/- under the Customs Act, 1962.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The matter relates to customs classification of certain goods imported by the Company’s Ennature Bio-Pharma division during the period June, 2020 to September 2024. The Company submitted a detailed reply to the allegations raised in the Show Cause Notice (“SCN”) issued by the Joint Commissioner of Customs, Air Cargo Complex (Import), Delhi. However, the adjudicating authority did not consider the submissions in the right prospective and confirmed the entire duty demand of Rs.32,95,005/- along with applicable interest and also imposed a penalty. The Company had already deposited the duty demand of Rs.32,96,284/- along with interest of Rs.11,22,338/- aggregating to Rs. 44,18,622/- under protest, before the issuance of SCN which has been appropriated towards the amount of short duty paid and interest thereon, by the adjudicating authority.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: Based on the Company’s assessment and advice of the counsel, the Company has a strong case on merits, and the imported goods were appropriately classified by the Company under CTH which has not been properly appreciated by the adjudicating authority. Accordingly, the Company will file the appeal and does not reasonably anticipate any material impact on its financial or operational or other activities.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Additional Commissioner Of Customs, Noida Customs Commissionerate
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs:
The Company vide its Letter dated 9th April,2024 has informed that the Company has received an Order from Additional Commissioner, Noida Customs Commissionerate, Uttar Pradesh, dated 22nd March, 2024 (received on 9th April, 2024) demanding an amount of Rs. 33.43 Crore as duty short paid along with applicable interest and imposing penalty of Rs. 82 Crore under the Customs Act, 1962. In the same order, redemption fine of Rs.191.76 Crore was also imposed on the goods already cleared during the period from 1st July 2017 to 1st February 2021.
Thereafter, an appeal against the said order was filed on7th June 2024, before the Commissioner of Customs (Appeals), GST Bhawan, Sector-48, Noida.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, E-Block, Nehru Colony, Haridwar Road, Dehradun, Uttarakhand (Commissioner).
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The Commissioner has filed an appeal challenging the order passed by the Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi (“CESTAT”), New Delhi, setting aside the Commissioner’s earlier order dated 9th May 2019. The Company has not yet received a notice from the Hon’ble High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital but was informed by its consultant after the matter appeared on the Court’s website. The matter pertains to the classification of 'RAB' under the Central Excise Tariff for the financial years 2005 to 2009. The CESTAT has already adjudicated in favor of the Company against the order of the Commissioner. Central Excise Duty amounting to Rs.10,39,32,564/- along with applicable interest and penalty. As the Company has already been awarded a favorable order on this matter by CESTAT, hence the Company, post discussions with the experts, believes that the above demand is not maintainable.
